title: Radar timeline opens on the OLDEST frame, so the Weather screen shows two-hour-stale cloud by default
reasoning: The claimed code is present and the Weather-screen half of the fixer's change is genuinely wired, but as SHIPPED the fix picked the frame by LIST POSITION and covered only one of the two surfaces that select a radar frame. Two gaps, both independently re-established here from source. (1) MISSED SURFACE: packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/weather/dashboard_weather_widget.dart:494 took `weatherStatus.radarFrames.first` under a comment reading 'Get the first radar frame (most recent)' — false for exactly the providers the fixer's own doc cites. That single _RadarPreview class is used by BOTH the Medium (300-450px) and Expanded (>450px) dashboard layouts, i.e. the radar an operator glances at without opening the Weather screen, so it still showed cloud up to two hours old. Same defect, second copy, untouched by the fix. (2) INVERSION ON THE NEWEST-FIRST PATH: the shipped helper scanned from the END of the list on the assumption 'providers hand back frames oldest -> newest'. NoaaRadarProvider does not. I read it directly: noaa_radar_provider.dart:347-348 does `timestamps.sort((a, b) => b.compareTo(a))` before `.take(_maxFrames)`, the frame list is then built by iterating `timestamps` in that order (fetchRadarFrames: `for (final timestamp in timestamps) frames.add(await _decodeFrame(...))`), and the fallback path `_generateFallbackTimestamps` also walks backwards from now — so NOAA's NEWEST frame is `frames.first` on both paths. Nothing re-sorts in between: WeatherRadarService.fetchRadarFrames caches and returns `fetched.withProviderName(...)` verbatim, weatherRadarFramesProvider returns `result.frames`, weatherStatusProvider copies it. Every NOAA frame is built with `isForecast: false` (both the no-data and decoded RadarFrame constructors), so the shipped helper returned frames.length-1 — the OLDEST. NOAA is reachable two ways: explicitly (_parseProviderType accepts 'noaa' from Settings) and by failover (WeatherRadarService walks failoverCandidates in priority order and takes the first success, so a GOES outage lands on NOAA). Note I do NOT endorse the framing that NOAA is the first auto choice — RadarProviderFactory.autoPriority is [goesSatellite, noaa, rainviewer, openmeteo, metno]; the 'NOAA > RainViewer > OpenMeteo' text in that file's doc comment is stale. That weakens the exposure but not the defect. RESIDUAL I FOUND AND DID NOT REPAIR (pre-existing, not caused by this fix, and the clean fix is in shared code — see blockedOnSharedCode): the same newest-first ordering also reverses the scrubber's TIME AXIS. _TimelineTrackPainter places every tick, the NOW marker, the progress fill and the thumb at `index * segmentWidth`, and _advanceFrame is `(i + 1) % n`, so on a newest-first provider the track reads right-to-left in time, 'Next frame' steps BACKWARDS in time and the play loop animates the weather in reverse. Order-dependence in this widget is the same root cause the fix's own doc comment now names.
evidence: Sever proof #1 (the fixer's own wiring): replacing `(_selectedFrameIndex ?? latestObservedRadarFrameIndex(radarFrames))` with `(_selectedFrameIndex ?? 0)` at weather_screen.dart:287 turned 2 tests red — 'the timeline opens on the newest frame, not the oldest' (Found 0 widgets with text 'Frame 13 of 13') and 'a nowcast tail does not drag the opening frame into the future' (Found 0 widgets with text 'Frame 10 of 13'); green on restore. The production call site is load-bearing, not decorative. Sever proof #2 (the helper repair): restoring the shipped reverse-scan body (`for (var i = frames.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) if (!frames[i].isForecast) return i;`) turned 'a reverse-chronological NOAA loop still opens on the newest' red (Found 0 widgets with text 'Frame 1 of 13') and the pure test 'picks by timestamp, not by list position' red (Expected <0>, Actual <5>); green on restore. Sever proof #3 (the dashboard repair): restoring `frames.first` turned the DashboardWeatherWidget test red — Expected 2026-08-09 13:27:01, Actual 2026-08-09 12:37:01, a 50-minute-stale thumbnail; green on restore. File is 9/9 green as it stands. Zone check (my own, not inherited): the all-forecast fallback compares `frame.timestamp.difference(DateTime.now())`, and Dart's DateTime.difference/isAfter compare absolute microsecondsSinceEpoch, so the documented provider zone split (RainViewer/NOAA build local-zoned instants, Open-Meteo builds UTC) cannot skew the choice. Second-copy hunt: the only remaining positional frame picks in non-test code are radar_timeline_scrubber.dart:292 (`frames.first` on the length==1 static path — correct, one frame) and apps/desktop/lib/headless_api/handlers/weather_handlers.dart:193 (`frames.first` used only as the seed of an explicit nearest-to-now loop — correct). CloudMotionAnalyzer does its own `..sort((a,b) => a.timestamp.compareTo(b.timestamp))` at line 139, so cloud-motion direction is NOT affected by provider ordering. Regression sweep under the repo's real gate: `flutter test --exclude-tags golden test/screens/framing test/screens/imaging/tabs test/screens/weather test/widgets/weather test/widgets/slew_dropdown_button_test.dart` = 196 tests, All tests passed. Without the exclusion 7 fail, all of them golden-tagged pixel captures whose baselines are dated Jun 5 and are gitignored (.gitignore:302 `**/test/**/captures/`, :305 `**/captures_landscape_test.dart`); melos.yaml:318 runs `--exclude-tags golden`. Honesty limit: the NOAA ordering is established from source and from a NOAA-shaped fixture, not from a live NEXRAD fetch — that would need network plus a US site.
repairSummary: The repair was already present in the working tree when I picked up this shard (landed by the earlier pass over the same shard ~20 minutes before); I re-derived the defect from source and re-proved the repair by severing each production line rather than re-authoring it. What is in the tree and verified: (a) latestObservedRadarFrameIndex in radar_timeline_scrubber.dart:29-53 selects the observed frame with the maximum TIMESTAMP (falling back to the frame nearest to now when every frame is a forecast), which is correct for ascending providers (RainViewer, Open-Meteo, MET Norway) and descending ones (NOAA) alike, with the ordering hazard recorded in the doc comment; (b) _RadarPreview in dashboard_weather_widget.dart:498-501 resolves through the same helper instead of `.first`, and the false 'first == most recent' comment is gone; (c) test/screens/weather/weather_screen_opens_on_now_test.dart carries a NOAA-shaped newest-first case driven through the real WeatherScreen, a pure-helper ordering case, and a DashboardWeatherWidget case asserting on WeatherRadarMap.currentFrame.timestamp. I verified each of the three fails when its production line is reverted and passes when restored, and left the tree byte-identical to how I found it.

title: The Slew split-button's primary half does nothing - every slew costs two clicks through a menu
reasoning: The headline claim is true and fixed at the cause. slew_dropdown_button.dart:118-205 is now a real split button: a Row of SkotiqButton whose onPressed calls _handleSlewMode(SlewMode.slew) directly, beside a PopupMenuButton carrying only the chevron. The IgnorePointer / ExcludeSemantics / `onPressed: enabled ? () {} : null` costume is gone from the file, and a repo-wide grep for `onPressed: () {}` / `onPressed: enabled ? () {}` / `onTap: () {},` across every package and app lib returns nothing, so no second copy of the antipattern survives. Safety is genuinely preserved rather than merely asserted: every entry point still funnels through _handleSlewMode, which runs _confirmHorizon() BEFORE the single-flight latch, and the five horizon-gate tests now drive the primary half — severing the primary's callback turns all five red. Both call sites were checked for layout, not assumed: mount_tab.dart:422-441 puts it in an Expanded half-Row beside Sync, framing_actions_panel.dart:315-317 in SizedBox(width: double.infinity); both bounded, so the Expanded inside Row(mainAxisSize: min) cannot throw. Where it fell short is the fixer's own stated sub-claim. The summary says 'the chevron gained symmetric padding so it is a real tap target instead of a bare 16px glyph'. As shipped (EdgeInsets.symmetric(horizontal: 6, vertical: 10) around a 16dp glyph) the PopupMenuButton measured 28.0 x 36.0 against SkotiqTokens.minTouchTarget = 48.0 — under the design system's minimum in BOTH axes. Splitting the control is what made that matter: the chevron became the ONLY route to Slew & Center and Slew, Center & Rotate, the plate-solved and rotated slews an operator reaches for when framing, so the fix pushed the precision paths behind a sub-minimum target. That is the fix half-landed, not a fresh defect. Two things I could not settle without a person, and I am not calling either a defect: the framing panel's one-click default is now a BARE slew even when framingState.rotation is non-zero and a rotator is connected (framing_actions_panel.dart:321-323 still passes targetRotation), so 'Slew to Target' on the GoTo & Frame step silently ignores the composition angle the operator set — defensible as 'the primary half does the simple thing', but it is a product call, not a code call; and 48dp finger reachability itself is judged from measured logical pixels in a widget test, never from a touch device.
evidence: Sever proof #1 (the fixer's wiring): replacing `onPressed: enabled ? () => _handleSlewMode(SlewMode.slew) : null` at slew_dropdown_button.dart:128 with `onPressed: enabled ? () {} : null` turned 7 tests red — 'the primary half slews on ONE click, with no menu' (service.calls 0), 'slew is single-flight and old-host completion is discarded' (Found 0 widgets with text 'Working...'), and all five horizon-gate tests (no 'Target is below the horizon' dialog, no 'Target is below your horizon limit', slew count Expected <1> Actual <0>, 'Slew was not sent' absent); green on restore. The production call site is load-bearing. Sever proof #2 (the touch-target repair): restoring the shipped EdgeInsets.symmetric(horizontal: 6, vertical: 10) turned 'the chevron half meets the design system touch minimum' red at Expected >= 48.0, Actual 28.0; green on restore. Independent measurement (my own probe, not inherited): with the repair in place the PopupMenuButton renders exactly Size(48.0, 48.0) at every parent width I tried — 120, 140, 158, 180, 220, 300 and 430dp — with the framing call site's real label ('Slew to Target') and icon, and tester.takeException() was null at all seven widths, so the 20dp the primary half gave up does not overflow even at 120dp (SkotiqButton ellipsizes; primary measured 68x48 there). The prior pass only probed the default 'Slew' label, so this closes the narrower-label gap. Accessibility measured rather than assumed: with ensureSemantics the chevron produces ONE node — SemanticsNode(actions: [focus, tap], flags: [isButton, hasEnabledState, isEnabled, isFocusable, hasExpandedState], label: 'More slew options', tooltip: 'More slew options') — so the explicit Semantics wrapper does not create a duplicate unnamed button beside it, and the control is keyboard-focusable. Regression sweep: `flutter test --exclude-tags golden test/screens/framing test/screens/imaging/tabs test/screens/weather test/widgets/weather test/widgets/slew_dropdown_button_test.dart` = 196 tests, All tests passed; slew_dropdown_button_test.dart alone is 14/14. The 7 failures visible without the golden exclusion are all pixel-capture goldens (framing/weather captures_landscape_test.dart, framing_registration_test.dart, framing_hips_layer_wiring_test.dart) whose baselines are dated Jun 5 and are gitignored dev artifacts excluded from `melos run test` (melos.yaml:318). I note honestly that framing/captures_landscape baselines WOULD now legitimately differ because the chevron widened by 20dp — but those files and their baselines are untracked and not part of any gate.
repairSummary: The repair was already present in the working tree when I picked up this shard; I re-measured the shipped 28x36 by reverting the repair, confirmed the touch-target test goes red at Actual 28.0, and restored. What is in the tree and verified: packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/slew_dropdown_button.dart:191-201 replaces the Padding(6, 10) with ConstrainedBox(minWidth/minHeight: SkotiqTokens.minTouchTarget), giving a measured 48x48 hit box with the 16dp glyph centred, no change to the control's overall height (the row was already 48 tall from the primary half) and no change to either call site's layout; test/widgets/slew_dropdown_button_test.dart carries 'the chevron half meets the design system touch minimum' (asserts both axes against the token) and 'both halves fit the narrow half-row mount_tab gives them' (renders at 158dp and asserts no layout exception). I added no new permanent test because my seven-width / real-label / semantics probe found nothing the two existing tests do not already pin; the probe file was deleted and the tree left byte-identical to how I found it. Not repaired, flagged for a product decision: whether the framing panel's one-click default should stay a bare slew when a rotation and a connected rotator are present.
